senses.definition: (New Zealand, derogatory) An inexperienced new worker, usually an immigrant.

quotes.text: Willie Cox said they found him in the barn, shot bang through the head, and the young English johnny who'd been on the station learning farming - disappeared.

senses.definition: (New England) A hospital gown: a gown with a back opening closed with snaps or ties, worn by hospital patients.

quotes.text: His hand shook. A little water spilled down the front of the hospital johnny Sean wore.

senses.definition: (US, slang, dated) Synonym of john: a toilet, lavatory, outhouse, or chamber pot.
examples: The women's toilet (as distinguished from the ladies' room in a speakeasy, the johnny at school, the little girls' room at a party in an apartment, and the wash-my-hands on a train) was clean enough.

quotes.text: Kitty Hofman came in the johnny.
quotes.reference: 1935, John O'Hara, chapter IV, in Appointment in Samarra, page 98:

senses.definition: (Ireland, slang, archaic) A half-glass of whisky.

quotes.text: [H]e declared, like a real Irishman, that 'if he were a living man when he died, he would not give a single johnny of whisky either at his wake or his funeral.'
